cards.explanation: The answer is sorrow. Baruch says, “Woe is me because the LORD has added sorrow to my pain!” (Jeremiah 45:3) So he was already hurting, and he says more got piled on top. I think that's a tired man talking, friends, and the LORD doesn't brush it aside. He quotes Baruch's own words right back to him.

The answer is True. Baruch says, “I am worn out with groaning and have found no rest.” (Jeremiah 45:3) Those are his words, and the LORD repeats them to him. I think anybody who has lain awake at 3 a.m. knows that feeling, friends. It's honest, and it's right there in the text.

The answer is demolish. The LORD says, “Throughout the land I will demolish what I have built and uproot what I have planted.” (Jeremiah 45:4) That's the LORD speaking about what He Himself built and planted. Big words, bakers, and the verse doesn't soften them. It's a heavy line, and the passage lets it stand.

The answer is great things for himself. The LORD asks, “But as for you, do you seek great things for yourself?” (Jeremiah 45:5) The question is aimed straight at Baruch, by name. It's a short question, friends, and I think it lands hard. The text doesn't say what those great things were, so I'll leave that open too.

The answer is False. The LORD asks, “But as for you, do you seek great things for yourself? Stop seeking!” (Jeremiah 45:5) That's the opposite of keep reaching. It's a short command, bakers, and the text doesn't add anything to it. The LORD speaks it to Baruch directly.

The answer is every living creature. The LORD says, “For I will bring disaster on every living creature, declares the LORD…” (Jeremiah 45:5) That's a wide net, friends, and the verse doesn't narrow it down. It's a heavy line, and I won't joke about it.

The answer is life. The LORD says, “…wherever you go, I will grant your life as a spoil of war.” (Jeremiah 45:5) After the heavy news, that's what Baruch is promised, friends. A spoil of war is what a person carries away from the fight. It's his life, and the LORD is the one who grants it.
